resolved_by: Sentencing Commission commentary: Application Note 14 to U.S.S.G. § 2K2.1, which the opinion says was added to resolve the split
issue: Under U.S.S.G. § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B), must the 'another felony offense' be distinct in time or conduct from the offense of conviction, or is it enough that it is a separate chargeable felony with different elements?

sides.position: The other felony must be distinct in time or conduct from the offense of conviction.
cases: United States v. Fenton, 309 F.3d 825 (3d Cir. 2002)
United States v. McDonald, 165 F.3d 1032 (6th Cir. 1999)
United States v. Szakacs, 212 F.3d 344 (7th Cir. 2000)

sides.position: The other felony need only be a separate offense with distinct elements (an elements test, e.g., Blockburger); a temporal or conduct distinction is not required.
cases: United States v. Blount, 337 F.3d 404 (4th Cir. 2003)
United States v. Luna, 165 F.3d 316 (5th Cir. 1999)
United States v. Kenney, 283 F.3d 934 (8th Cir. 2002)

this_court: Adopts the elements-based position (a distinct chargeable crime), consistent with Application Note 14; United States v. McIntosh, 124 F.4th 199 (3d Cir. 2024), itself supports this reading.
quote: After all, Note 14 was added to resolve a growing circuit split.
cite: United States v. Nahsiem McIntosh, 124 F.4th 199 (3rd Cir. 2024)
